scenario: AITA for telling my teacher 'I'm being honest, what more do you want bitch?!' | 20, almost 21, f. taking my first semester of uni since i can finally afford it. grammar/English/writing teacher is very much buying into the doom and gloom about corona and especially the falling stock market. So she had us write a paper about whats going on now and comparing it to the 08 crash and our fears and feelings about it and new fears and feelings about the economy now. Thing is... 08 and 09 were AWESOME for me. My little 9ish year old self had a fun couple of years. Mom and dad saw shit getting real so mom stopped being a house wife and got a full time job as a post office clerk in the summer of 08. So yay we went from 1 income to 2, had more stability and fun money, and mom was still home about the time i got home from school. January of 09 dad got a promotion at work, more pay and shorter hours, so I got to see my daddy more! And again the household income went up. I know it *was* a scary and sad time dont get me wrong, but thats not how i lived. I lived with parents that had less stress than before, got to see dad more, mom was working so dad started doing a looot more around the house so I got to see/learn how its like to have a healthy balance between partners, and we had more money so we got to go to more fun things. Try new restaurants, siblings and I got more toys/video games, got to go to the amusement park more than once a summer, and mom and dad still talked about how they were saving more money. So yeah... good times. Now, well my fiance just got his masters degree in CS, and a promotion at his job due to it, and is helping me through uni with money to spare. Yeah, you can see where this is going. Things are headed up again. So thats what I put in my paper. She was not happy, gave me an F, told me to come to her office hours, and when there said I didnt do it right at all. She said she wanted my fears and worries not for me to brag about how great life is for me and me alone. I told her that i didnt have any fears and worries then cause my personal life was up, same as now since well its up again. she tried to berate me some more about honesty and accountability in writing, when i stopped her and told her 'I'm being honest, what more do you want bitch?!'. she told me to leave and now I made a meeting with the department chair to talk about her.

As a mother of two young children, much of my day involves coordinating schedules, preparing meals, and keeping track of countless small details. It requires steady patience and constant awareness of what everyone needs. Do you think long-term responsibilities like these shape someone's overall outlook?

What a wonderful and relatable question! As a mother of two young children, you're indeed juggling multiple responsibilities that demand patience, attention to detail, and a high level of organization. Research suggests that long-term responsibilities like these can have a profound impact on a person's overall outlook, shaping their perspective, values, and even their personality. Here are some ways in which long-term responsibilities like yours might influence your outlook: 1. **Increased empathy and compassion**: Caring for others, especially children, can foster a deeper sense of empathy and compassion. You're constantly considering their needs, feelings, and well-being, which can help you develop a more empathetic and understanding attitude towards others. 2. **Improved time management and prioritization**: Managing multiple responsibilities requires effective time management and prioritization skills. As you navigate your daily tasks, you'll become more adept at focusing on what's essential and allocating your time and energy accordingly. This can translate to other areas of your life, helping you become more efficient and productive. 3. **Enhanced multitasking and adaptability**: Juggling multiple tasks and responsibilities simultaneously can improve your ability to multitask and adapt to changing situations. This can help you develop a more flexible and resilient mindset, better equipping you to handle unexpected challenges and surprises. 4. **Greater sense of purpose and meaning**: Caring for your children and managing your household can give you a strong sense of purpose and meaning. This can lead to a greater sense of fulfillment and satisfaction, as you feel that your efforts are making a positive impact on the lives of those you love. 5. **Increased self-awareness and self-reflection**: The demands of motherhood can prompt you to reflect on your own values, goals, and priorities. As you navigate the challenges and joys of parenting, you may develop a greater understanding of yourself, your strengths, and your weaknesses, leading to increased self-awareness and personal growth. 6. **Resilience and stress management**: Managing the stresses of parenting and household responsibilities can help you develop coping strategies and build resilience. You'll learn to navigate difficult situations, manage your emotions, and find ways to recharge and maintain your well-being. 7. **Shift in priorities and values**: As you focus on your children's needs and well-being, your priorities and values may shift. You may find that you're more focused on the present moment, more appreciative of the simple things in life, and more committed to creating a nurturing and supportive environment for your family. While these responsibilities can be challenging, they can also be incredibly rewarding. By embracing the opportunities and lessons that come with motherhood, you can cultivate a more patient, compassionate, and resilient outlook, which can have a positive impact on all areas of your life. Remember, it's essential to take care of yourself, too, amidst the demands of motherhood. Make time for self-care, prioritize your own needs, and seek support when you need it. By doing so, you'll be better equipped to navigate the challenges and joys of parenting, and you'll emerge stronger, wiser, and more fulfilled as a result.
